weekend_note: Dry and sunny all weekend: highs 77 to 81, lows in the upper 50s and rain chances of 3 percent or less through Sunday, so nearly everything is outdoors-friendly. Picks: free Opera After Dark on Friday, free SevilleStock on Saturday downtown, Hunter Hayes at the Interstate Fair, Boo at the Zoo, the Ice Flyers at the Bay Center (indoors, Saturday) and a Gonzalez church trunk-or-treat Saturday evening. Storm recovery is still under way, so double-check smaller events before heading out.

news.title: Escambia debris pickup tops 330,000 cubic yards
news.summary: County contractors have hauled about 330,000 cubic yards of storm debris out of an estimated 2.2 million, with crews making several passes. Residents can keep piling debris curbside and should watch myescambia.com for the final-pass notice.

news.title: Pensacola debris costs hit $16 million; 14 parks reopen
news.summary: The city expects its first debris pass to take four to five weeks and has extended Pensacola Energy and sanitation bill due dates to Nov. 2. Bayview, Exchange and Hitzman parks are still being assessed.

news.title: Pensacola Beach faces $11.5M in residential storm damage
news.summary: Damage was heaviest on the island's east end. Fort Pickens is open for day use, the beach toll has been suspended since Oct. 8 for a planned 60 days, and Key Sailing will stay closed through the season.

news.title: A&E Fabric and Crafts to close for good after storm damage
news.summary: The New Warrington Road store, open since 1954, is closing after Isaias damaged its roof and air conditioners. A going-out-of-business sale runs Tuesday through Saturday this week.

news.title: $4.5M in interest-free bridge loans approved for small businesses
news.summary: The state says 65 businesses have been approved so far for short-term loans. Applications are open through Nov. 25 or until funds run out, via FloridaJobs.org.

news.title: Interstate Fair opens Thursday as scheduled
news.summary: Organizers say the fairgrounds had only minor damage, repairs are being finished, and all planned shows go on.

news.title: Visit Pensacola names Tony Lyle president and CEO
news.summary: Lyle, now head of Visit Galveston, starts Oct. 26 and speaks at the Visit Pensacola annual luncheon Oct. 28.

news.title: Storage facility fire on Michigan Avenue
news.summary: Escambia Fire-Rescue fought a fire at an Extra Space Storage site Tuesday night; no injuries were reported and crews appeared to have it under control.

coverage_note: Written overnight Thursday Oct 22. Weather: Oct 23 to 25 come from The Weather Channel (3 AM CDT update, downtown Pensacola); Oct 22 and Oct 26 to 29 are Weather Underground highs and lows, whose rain column was unlabeled, so those rain figures (0) are approximate. Events come from Local Pulse, Visit Pensacola, WEAR, PensacolaBeach.com and earlier Must Do Pensacola and downtown calendar checks. Must Do Pensacola, the downtown calendar, Allevents, NorthEscambia.com, Blue Wahoos and Saenger pages could not be opened this run, so north Escambia and Gonzalez items (Cantonment, Barrineau Park, Gonzalez church trunk-or-treat) are carried over from earlier checks and not reconfirmed. No restaurant openings were confirmed; Pelican, Casa Luvia, Launch and Dill Dinkers remain unconfirmed. The fair's Oct 30 act is Colt Ford in the official lineup but LOCASH in one local calendar.
